[EFFECT] Holidays have a negative effect on predicted hourly bike demand. When the value is near 0 (non-holiday), the contribution is essentially neutral (close to zero), but when the value is near 1 (a holiday), the contribution drops to about −0.14 in log space, which means roughly 13–15% fewer bikes rented than on a typical non-holiday hour. The effect is essentially a downward step: demand is slightly suppressed on holidays compared to regular days.

[IMPORTANCE] "Holiday" is the least important feature in the model, ranked 9th out of 9 features with an importance score of only 0.008. Its influence on predicted demand is very small relative to factors like hour of the day, temperature, or weather.

[RECOMMENDATION] Because the effect of holidays on demand is small but consistently negative, planners can make a modest reduction in bike availability or staffing on public holidays, while keeping in mind that other factors — especially the time of day — will have a far greater impact on how many bikes are actually needed.
